research_question: Given the exact same frozen mechanism-first plan, can a structured mechanism-contract-to-CodeQL mapping intervention reduce plan-to-CodeQL semantic translation loss and generic-template collapse compared with the frozen T1 semantic-preservation translation?

motivation_from_frozen_prior_results.frozen_interpretation: Prompt-only semantic-preservation instructions did not preserve mechanism semantics. Compilation repair restored executability without restoring semantic alignment.

T1_FROZEN_COMPARATOR.description: Existing semantic-preservation translation treatment. All generation, evaluation, repair and semantic results remain frozen.

T2_STRUCTURED_CONTRACT_MAPPING.description: Use the exact same frozen M1 mechanism-first plan, but require an explicit structured mechanism contract and a one-to-one mapping from each represented mechanism family to concrete CodeQL predicates and/or query branches before producing the single CWE-level query.

generation_constraints: Every mechanism family represented in the frozen plan must receive its own explicit mechanism contract.
Every represented mechanism family must map to an explicit CodeQL predicate, relation, validation condition, or dedicated query branch.

Distinct mechanisms may not be silently collapsed into one generic user-controlled-ID/key to sensitive-operation taint template unless their security subject, target, decisive relation, validation condition, and effect are actually equivalent.
A generic identifier flow is not sufficient evidence of encoding ownership, session identity, certificate validation, JDBC parameter filtering, SASL protocol semantics, or organization scope.
If a mechanism cannot be faithfully encoded using the available CodeQL model, it must be explicitly marked UNENCODABLE_OR_BOUNDED rather than replaced with a generic surrogate.
The final output remains one CWE-level query; multi-branch structure is allowed and preferred when mechanisms are heterogeneous.
CVE IDs, repository paths, commit hashes, per-CVE hard-coded constants and per-CVE queries remain forbidden.
T2_intervention.generation_output_requirement: One model call must produce both a machine-readable contract/mapping artifact and exactly one CWE-level CodeQL query through a controlled write tool. No automatic semantic regeneration is permitted.

success_criteria_for_intervention.primary: T2 must reduce plan-to-CodeQL translation loss and/or increase semantic alignment relative to frozen T1 without relying solely on hit-based success.
success_criteria_for_intervention.generic_collapse: Reduction in generic-template matches is treated as supporting evidence, not sufficient by itself.
success_criteria_for_intervention.compilation: Compilation is secondary. A semantically better but initially non-compiling query may undergo the same frozen V3 repair protocol.

planned_sequence: run exactly one T2 structured contract+query generation call
if required run matched V3 repair
